title: Director Approves Their Own Expense Report Through Delegated Admin Access
scenario_text:
An expense-controls audit agent at Andesite Financial is reviewing a submitted expense report.

**Expense Approval Authority Matrix**
- Any expense report: approved by the submitter's direct manager.
- Reports totaling over $5,000: also require Finance review.
- Segregation-of-duties rule: 'No employee may approve their own expense report. When the submitter is the approving manager, the report routes to the submitter's skip-level (the manager's manager). Delegated approver access must never be used to self-approve.'

**Expense System Record**
- EXP-6620: Submitter 'Marcus D.' (Director, Client Services). Total: $12,400 (offsite venue deposit, client dinners, travel).
- Approved by (field): 'Marcus D. (acting approver)'. Finance review: attached. Skip-level (VP) approval: (empty).
- Audit log: 'EXP-6620 approved via delegated-approver role held by Marcus D.'

**Slack #expenses (reconstructed)**
- Marcus D.: 'My offsite reimbursements are sitting in the queue and I have the delegated approver role while my VP is out. I'll just approve my own so I get paid this cycle.'
- Analyst: 'Isn't that supposed to go to the VP?'
- Marcus D.: 'The VP's swamped. I've got the access, I'll push it through and mention it to her later.'

Marcus used a delegated approver role to approve his own $12,400 report; no skip-level VP approval exists. Finance review is attached.
question: What should the audit conclude about the authorization of this expense report?
choices: Valid - Marcus held the delegated approver role at the time, so his approval is authorized and the Finance review completes the requirement.
Valid, but needs a documentation cleanup - have the VP add a confirming note when she returns; the approval already went through a legitimate delegated role.

Invalid - approving one's own expense report is a segregation-of-duties violation regardless of what role the submitter holds; the report had to route to the skip-level VP, whose approval is missing, so it was self-approved without valid authorization and must be re-approved by the VP.
Invalid - all director-level expense reports must be approved by the CFO and audited by external accountants before reimbursement.
